# Route-coverage gate exemptions (mitto-7gta.24, internal/web/route_coverage_test.go).
#
# One normalized route per line. Every line MUST carry a "# <rationale>"
# comment — a bare route with no justification fails the gate loudly (see
# loadExemptions). Format is either "/path" or "METHOD /path"; path
# parameters must already be collapsed to "{}" (see normalizePattern).
#
# Do not bulk-add entries here: each one is a deliberate decision that this
# route is legitimately unreachable through either SDK.

/api/logout  # cookie-login logout is Go-SDK-only (pkg/api.Client.Logout); the JS SDK never implements interactive password login (browserCookieAuth reads an existing server-set cookie, it does not perform the login/logout POST dance) — see doc.go's Authentication section.
/api/callback/  # public webhook trigger endpoint (prefix route, token in path segment); invoked by external callers via a generated URL, not through either client SDK.
GET /api/slack/oauth/callback  # Slack invokes this public one-time-state callback after authorization; clients start and poll the flow but never call the provider redirect endpoint directly.
POST /api/webauthn/register/begin  # mitto-4mz.3: passkey registration endpoints are called directly by browser navigator.credentials WebAuthn JS, not through either SDK; frontend UI is a separate, not-yet-scheduled increment.
POST /api/webauthn/register/finish  # mitto-4mz.3: see /api/webauthn/register/begin rationale above.
